Identifying phase separation modulators mediated by the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein using a structure-based drug discovery approach.

This study uses a structure-based drug discovery approach to identify small molecules that modulate phase separation driven by the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein, a viral mechanism not targeted by current antivirals. The work aims to find new therapeutic candidates that could remain effective as the virus evolves and acquires resistance to existing drugs.

GolgiFold: A Structural Predictome of Human Golgi Protein Complexes.

GolgiFold presents a systematic structural predictome of human Golgi protein complexes, using computational structure prediction to map molecular assemblies across the Golgi interactome. The work aims to define complexes for the many Golgi-associated proteins whose assemblies remain uncharacterized, potentially revealing unrecognized components and regulatory mechanisms in Golgi trafficking and homeostasis.

Domain-Aware Enzyme Classification via Multiple Instance Learning.

The paper introduces a domain-aware enzyme classification method that uses multiple instance learning to focus on local functional regions (e.g., catalytic residues and domains) rather than whole-sequence embeddings, avoiding dependence on accurate 3D structures. This addresses limitations of existing protein language model and structure-based EC number prediction approaches, aiming to improve protein function annotation and metabolic pathway reconstruction.

Structural clustering across the tree of life reveals candidate Asgard-eukaryote homologs and a shared expansion of solenoids.

This study takes a family-level approach to structural clustering across the tree of life, analyzing 1.89 million structural clusters from the AFESM database to profile their taxonomic composition. By starting from protein families rather than individual Asgard proteins, the authors identify candidate Asgard-eukaryote homologs and uncover a shared expansion of solenoid protein folds. The work expands the known repertoire of eukaryotic signature proteins in Asgard archaea and provides a complementary method for deep homology detection.

Discovery of benzimidazole-based selective α-glucosidase inhibitors with an uncompetitive mode of action: synthesis, biological assays and computational studies.

The authors synthesized thirteen benzimidazole derivatives and tested them as α-glucosidase inhibitors, finding that a chlorine at the C-6 position plus appropriate aromatic substituents boosts activity. Compounds 6 and 13 were the most potent (IC50 32.35 and 15.70 μM), outperforming acarbose (139 μM), and compound 13 acts via an uncompetitive inhibition mode. Computational docking and dynamics studies supported the structure-activity relationships.

Distance-AF Multimer is a new computational pipeline that incorporates user-provided distance constraints between residues into protein complex structure prediction. The approach offers a way to leverage sparse experimental restraints to improve complex modeling.

Free-Energy and Molecular Dynamics Analysis of Ser195 and Thr195 Rotameric States in Thrombin.

This study uses well-tempered metadynamics and microsecond molecular dynamics simulations to compare the conformational energetics of serine versus threonine at position 195 in thrombin. The authors find that S195 and T195 occupy distinct rotameric free-energy landscapes, with S195 preferring a lower-angle rotamer in the apo state, offering a molecular explanation for why serine is strongly conserved over threonine at this catalytic nucleophile position in trypsin-like serine proteases.

Edge-Aware Graph Attention Networks for Interpreting Biophysical Mechanisms from Molecular Dynamics Simulations.

This preprint introduces three edge-aware graph attention network variants (Edge-Conditioned, Edge-Injected, Edge-Gated) for learning biomolecular dynamics from molecular dynamics simulations, with the goal of extracting mechanistic insight from learned attention. The edge-aware models reportedly improve prediction performance over a standard GAT and allow attention-derived communication networks to be interpreted as biophysical mechanisms. It is a methods contribution aimed at making AI models of MD more interpretable.

Structural Basis for Angiotensin II Type I Receptor G Protein-biased Signaling.

This preprint reports cryo-EM structures of the angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) bound to G protein with either the natural ligand angiotensin II or the G protein-biased agonist TRV055. The two ligands adopt similar poses but trigger coordinated structural rearrangements that propagate from the ligand-binding pocket to the intracellular surface, revealing how biased signaling is encoded. These structures provide a template for designing safer cardiovascular drugs that preferentially activate G protein rather than β-arrestin pathways.

The goal is to block autoantibody-driven AT1R activation in autoimmune cardiovascular and renal disease while sparing physiological AngII signaling. From prediction to creation: How AI-driven design is reshaping microbial biocatalysis.

This review argues that AI-driven protein design has moved beyond structure prediction toward generative creation of novel enzymes, using the largely uncharacterised microbial world as both a source of sequence diversity and a set of expression hosts. It surveys three stages: mining microbial sequence space, generative design of new biocatalysts, and the organism-agnostic nature of these tools. The key message is that AI is shifting enzyme engineering from being bounded by natural enzyme space to designing catalysts that do not exist in nature.

This resource supports structure-based drug discovery by providing a unified, structure-centered view of biologically relevant interactions.

InterPro: the protein sequence classification resource in 2027.
